recon.notes: Eventbrite organizer page, confirmed as a Next.js page by the working __NEXT_DATA__ payload (not by CSS). Megawoof America is an LA-based touring party, so city/timezone/bar/location are set per event from primary_venue.address and no city default is used. The organizer block publishes no website/instagram/facebook (organizer.website etc. are absent from the payload; no linktr.ee/instagram/megawoof domain string appears in any of the four HTMLs), so those defaults are null. The Bear Calendar aggregator republishes these three events; that cross-listing belongs in the-bear-calendar's file, not here. Run 20260909-072307 already returns all three with the right dates and bars (the SF record has no bar).

coverage.basis: Feed door (__NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps): upcomingEvents 3 rows, hasMoreUpcoming false, upcomingEventsTotal 3 — the feed's own completeness flag says there is nothing to page. Second listing door (headless Chrome DOM of the same URL) shows exactly the same three cards. Each of the three event pages was opened and its JSON-LD agrees with the feed row on title, date, start time, venue and address, and adds the end times the feed omits. All three rows have series_id null and additionalSessionsCount 0, so 3 cards = 3 dated singles, no series. Past listings: organizer.metrics.totalEvents is 106 lifetime, so 103 past events exist behind the client-loaded Past tab; they are not in the static payload, the /showmore endpoint 403s, and they are counted here, not enumerated. Three flyers were read and corroborate every date, venue and address (no years printed on any flyer; the year comes from the feed's start_date and JSON-LD).

traps.label: Past tab on the organizer page (103 past events behind it)
traps.why: The organizer header shows 'total events 106' lifetime against 3 upcoming, so 103 past listings exist. They are client-loaded on the Past tab, absent from the static __NEXT_DATA__ payload, and the /org/<id>/showmore/ endpoint returns 403 — they are not reachable from the configured door and must not be counted as missing events. Past occurrences of the same city stops (Chicago, San Diego, SF, LA, etc.) are the classic source of stale duplicates if a cached page from an earlier month is ever replayed.

traps.label: 'More events from Megawoof America' and 'You might also like...' sections on each event page
traps.why: Eventbrite appends organizer cross-sell and recommendation rails to every event page. In the static HTML they are empty prose shells ('Discover more events from Megawoof America...' / 'Browse more events with different dates, prices, and formats'); when rendered client-side they fill with other organizers' events in the same city. Nothing in them is a Megawoof listing that the organizer feed does not already carry.

traps.label: 'From $11.58' price line on each organizer card
traps.why: Every rendered card ends with a minimum ticket price (ticket_availability.minimum_ticket_price in the feed). It is a price tier, not an event, and the display value (16.84 USD with fees) differs from the card value (11.58) — neither is event data.

traps.label: 'SUPPORTING 11th ST. BEARRISON STREET FAIR' badge on the San Francisco flyer
traps.why: The SF flyer carries a Bearrison Street Fair logo and the title says 'BEARRISON WEEKEND'. Bearrison Street Fair is a separate daytime event run by another organizer; on this source it is only a sponsorship badge and a weekend label. An OCR pass must not turn it into a second event or into this event's venue (the venue is the STUD logo beside the Folsom address).

traps.label: 'THE HOLE' badge ('FEEL FRISKY DOWNSTAIRS') on the Chicago flyer
traps.why: The Hole is Jackhammer's downstairs bar; the flyer badge advertises a room inside the same venue on the same night, not a second event or a different venue. Bar for this event stays Jackhammer (feed primary_venue.name and JSON-LD location.name).

openQuestions.q: The SF row's venue name on Eventbrite is the street address '1123 Folsom St'; the bar name (The Stud) exists only as a logo on the flyer. Should the expectation for a text-only crawl be bar null, or is the flyer OCR path expected to recover 'The Stud'? Run 20260909-072307 returned this event with no bar.

Run 20260909-072307 attributes website https://linktr.ee/megawoof_america to all three events, but that string does not appear in the organizer payload or any of the three event pages. Where does the scraper get it (AI prior, The Bear Calendar merge, calendar enrich)?
